report:
The unchanged manuscript has a false unconditional supporting lemma, and the displayed endpoint does not satisfy the task’s explicit requirement of a nonseparable f. The principal contact arguments do check out in their actual PA PC applications. The original P05.2 classification is correctly left open, consistently with the permitted partial-paper scope.

The concrete mathematical defect is Lemma 3, “Strict affine floor.” Its preceding setup introduces a general PA function; neither its statement nor that setup assumes PC. Absence of a nonzero zero-cost positive relation does not imply positive relation costs. Take X=R with unit balanced edge weights, γ(x)=|x|, and the literal relative PA function f(x)=-|x| for |x|≤1 and f(x)=|x|-2 for |x|≥1. Its difference from γ is bounded. At zero, d₁=1, d₂=-1, s=(-1,-1), and K={(a,a):a≥0}. Every nonzero relation has cost -2a, so there is no flat relation. Nevertheless a strict floor ℓ(x)=bx would require b<-1 from the positive direction and b>1 from the negative direction. It cannot exist. The proof’s inference that the normalized minimum θ is positive omits s·λ≥0. B225 supplies positive spanning, not this slope inequality. An explicit PC hypothesis makes the intended lemma correct, and every subsequent contact application establishes that hypothesis; it does not validate the unconditional lemma in the unchanged TeX and native argument. Note n1’s PA PC qualification cannot silently amend those statements.

There is also an exact task-scope discrepancy. Write C=({y=0}∪{x=0})⊂R². Then X=C×R and the displayed endpoint is f(q,z)=F(q)+|z|, where F(q)=max(|x|,|y|-1,0). Thus f is separable on this product. The roof obstacle u is genuinely nonseparable: on the horizontal plane its values at (x,z)=(0,0),(R,0),(0,R),(R,R) are R,0,0,0, whose mixed difference is R. The manuscript establishes an obstruction with a nonseparable obstacle and a separable endpoint. It does not establish the task’s expressly requested nonseparable f. A different endpoint would require a new construction and proof.

I checked the external intersection dependencies against the complete publisher proof units: BBGS Definitions 3.2–3.9, Proposition 3.12, Proposition 3.15, Lemma 3.18 and Proposition 3.19. Their hypotheses admit real affine coefficients and arbitrary real weights, including zero intermediate weights. The source’s incorrect internal reference in Proposition 3.19’s commuting step is harmless: the equality follows from Proposition 3.15. [Publisher proof chain](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6.pdf).

Reconstructing the lattice conversion gives the stated operator. A saturated facet lattice followed by a primitive quotient lift is a basis of the cell lattice, so the projected height is aσ/aτ. Consequently cσ becomes the Euclidean weight aσcσ. Writing each primitive lift as its perpendicular part plus a tangent vector, continuity identifies the tangent slopes and balancing cancels their total contribution. Hence B₋f(ac)(τ)=aτD_fc(τ). This identity repeats at every recursive dimension; at vertices aᵥ=1. It gives the exact raw mass without an additional factorial. Tangent-lift changes cancel directly in the raw formula.

The codimension-two argument covers nonsimplicial cells: quotienting an actual codimension-two face leaves a pointed two-dimensional wedge with exactly two boundary rays. If their angle is θ, the perpendicular expansions have coefficients -cot θ and csc θ, exchanged by reflection. Grouping the two facet contributions gives symmetric diagonal and cross terms. Existing common lineality is removed in this quotient. Refinement compatibility includes all three dimensional cases: inherited facets retain their weights; new facets inside a weighted affine cell have opposite cancelling contributions; cells lying in old faces of greater dimension inherit zero weight. These facts apply to arbitrary common rational refinements. Linear-form annihilation then proves balanced preservation. Local supports prove nonnegativity at every recursive stage, even when some intermediate weights vanish. The real extension remains confined to finite PA intersections.

The complete caller grants were used within scope. B225 applies to inherited finite positive balanced stars: their saturated tangent spaces and primitive inward classes are unchanged, and top weights remain strictly positive. R230 applies to the finite-valued printed-PC class on this domain. A continuous PA PC function equals its completion and therefore satisfies real-endpoint PCC inequalities. Completion preserves a competitor’s actual upper growth bound because comparison with continuous γ+C passes from rational points to all points. A224 is context and motivation; its fan-specific obstruction and disclosed active-coefficient strictness convention are not promoted to general theorems.

The local-support and finite-support proofs otherwise check out. After subtracting a segment chord, a positive maximum would have a nonempty closed maximum set. At each maximum, a supporting affine slope must vanish, making that set open and contradicting connectedness. Thus supports imply convexity on every contained segment, and propagation from a PCC center gives every real-endpoint inequality. For PA divisors, a support agrees with the tangent slope on the center face; the correction cancels and every remaining inward slope is nonnegative.

At a rational face center, sufficiently small rational generator endpoints establish necessity directly from the printed PCC definition. The support duality is valid: active-column elimination leaves independent columns, whose inverse maps uniformly bound coefficients on finitely many subsets, proving that R₊ᵐ+im(Uᵀ) is closed. Nearest-point separation produces λ≥0, Uλ=0 and λ·s<0 whenever a support is infeasible. Extreme positive kernel rays have one-dimensional kernels on their supports; otherwise a small two-sided kernel perturbation destroys extremality. Their supports have size at most rank(U)+1, and rational elimination gives rational generators. Tests at rational representatives cover every real point of every shared face because tangent cones and affine slopes are unchanged throughout its relative interior. No ambient-global convex extension is needed.

For PC germs, the intended strict-floor proof is complete. Costs are nonnegative; absence of zero cost makes their minimum θ on the nonempty compact normalized kernel section positive. Taking 0<δ<θ and separating s-δ1 gives generator residuals at least δ. In fact c=δ/maxᵢ||dᵢ|| is a valid norm lower bound. Opposite lineality generators automatically give a flat relation. Genuine common lineality of the carrying cycle and affine germ forces zero top atom: the generalized carrying fan has no zero-dimensional faces, and refinement independence preserves that zero after artificial cuts. Mere affinity on an isolated line does not supply this stronger hypothesis.

The noncontact perturbation is valid in its actual application. The finite envelope is PC by the supremum inequalities, continuous because it is PA, and has the required growth bound. A positive obstacle gap persists on a small neighborhood. Choosing t below both that gap and cr/2 makes max(f,f(v)+t+ℓ) agree with f on a strict collar, remain below the obstacle and preserve growth. Local supports persist at active and tie points, so the modification is an allowed PC competitor raising the center. Its possibly irrational breakpoints cause no difficulty because competitors need not be PA.

The radial roof obstruction also checks out for an actual globally realized relative PA PC f. A sufficiently small rational sup-norm radius keeps every radial sector inside its incident affine cell and excludes other carrying vertices. The roof has integral slopes and rational constants. Scaling a flat relation to rational boundary endpoints preserves both the barycenter and zero average slope cost, forcing q(v)≤f(v) for every competitor. Rational radial chords then force q≤f inside the roof, and the obstacle gives that bound outside. Rational simplices in the minimal rational face extend it to every real point without assuming continuity of q. The resulting envelope is exactly f, has a constant decreasing regularization, and new subdivision vertices have zero raw mass. Its contact integral is exactly -Rmᵥ.

Accordingly, the corollary’s equivalence is established for a fixed PA PC reference and coefficient category, with all admissible PA obstacles whose actual envelopes themselves belong to the relative finite PAPC class. Its reverse direction quantifies actual global relative functions, not arbitrary local jets. It provides no extension to general non-PA regularizable endpoints, infinite refinements or the full original classification.

The fixed-structure certificate is valid within that scope. Shared-face continuity is tested on rational affine bases, and circuit inequalities are required at every face. Equality of all recession slopes is exactly bounded difference from the actual reference: necessity follows along rays; sufficiency follows from the bounded-point-plus-recession decomposition obtained by homogenization, retaining both signs of lineality. On a fixed structure the recursion gives a homogeneous degree-d polynomial in the slopes. Nonnegative extreme costs make a flat relation equivalent to a zero extreme cost, so adjoining positive raw mass gives the stated finite semialgebraic disjunction. Literal integrality and rational constants remain additional arithmetic restrictions. No uniform refinement bound or automatic local-germ realization follows.

The two-plane numerical mathematics is correct. The eight saturated unit-weight quadrants balance, and γ is a positive-growth ambient convex restriction. The displayed f is also an ambient convex restriction and f-γ lies in [-1,0]. For the conical germ carried by these quadrants, K has the three opposing-pair rays, PC is A,B,C≥0, first weights on x±,y±,z± are C,C,A+B, and the second mass is 2C(A+B). For f this is 8. Globally the first cycle has weight two on all three axes and weight one on each line (0,±1,z). At p±=(0,±1,0), weights 2,2,1,1 and slopes 0,1,1,1 give mass 4 each. Opposite directions balance at every vertex and there are no further atoms. The reference has sole mass 16. The radius-1/4 roof has exact unrestricted envelope f and contact integral -(1/4)·8=-2, independently of total-mass equality or competitor continuity.

The irrational-kink example is correct. Both individual functions belong to real PA on rational structures; their maximum is max(x,2t-x), with t=√2/2, and cannot have a finite rational carrying structure. Rational tₙ decreasing to t yield literal PA PC functions Hₙ with exact uniform error 2(tₙ-t), preserving bounded relative growth. Thus this maximum is literally regularizable despite failing PA_R membership. The listed rational upper brackets and error bounds are consistent. This proves neither general regularization nor a full original counterexample.

I separately checked the TeX, native argument, ledger and five unregistered notes as mathematical records. Harmless clarifications are the source’s commuting-reference correction, nonincreasing interpretation of decreasing sequences, the PA/common-structure restriction for divisor-support applications, and the malformed U₃,₄ bibliography notation in the native conversion. Adding PC to the unconditional strict-floor lemma changes its hypotheses; calling the separable f nonseparable changes the claimed scope. Neither correction is silently adopted here. Compiler results, finite-grid counts, hashes and registration records remain data. The failure “Unknown, dead, or forward support: B225” is preserved, with no canonical registered author result and no support-label repair. The mathematical verdict is independent of that operational failure.

passages.statement: On a Euclidean quasi-embedded polyhedral space X, for an open subset U and a common carrying complex Π, BBGS’s negative inward-unit-conormal product of real PA functions and arbitrary real weights commutes with restriction, subdivision and iterated products whenever defined. A weight is balanced iff its product with every ambient linear function vanishes; restriction, subdivision and PA products preserve balanced weights. Strict positivity is not required (BBGS Propositions 3.12, 3.15, 3.19 and Lemma 3.18).
